draft.title: Planning with Country and diverse communities
card: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples have cared for Country for tens of thousands of years. Country means the land, waters, plants, animals and sky, and the connections between them.
This knowledge can guide how a city is planned. Planners can work with local Aboriginal communities and Elders to learn how land and water have been cared for in that place.
In a new suburb, this can mean restoring a creek instead of piping it underground. It can also mean planting native species that suit the local soil and climate.
Planning also needs to include the views of other diverse communities, such as migrants, older people and people with disability. Each group may need different services and spaces.
draft.remember: Good planning listens to many communities, including Aboriginal knowledges of caring for Country.

a.q: Which action is an example of planning a new suburb with Aboriginal knowledges of caring for Country?
opts: Restoring a creek and planting local native species
Building a larger shopping centre beside the main road
Covering a creek with pipes to make more room for houses
Planting imported trees chosen for fast growth
a.why: Restoring a creek and planting local native species uses knowledge about how a place has been cared for over a long time. Piping a creek removes the waterway, so it does not care for Country.
a.clue: Which action looks after the local waters and plants?

b.q: A council plans a new suburb in Western Sydney. It wants the plan to include Aboriginal knowledges. Which step would best do this?
opts: Work with local Aboriginal Elders on caring for the creek
Name the streets after plants and then use standard designs
Use the same plan as another suburb in a different region
Ask only the developers to decide where the parks go
b.why: Working with local Elders brings in knowledge about that particular place, such as its waterways. Naming streets after plants is only a label. It does not change how the land and water are cared for.
b.clue: Which step involves people who hold knowledge of this place?

a.best: Restoring a creek and planting local native species

b.best: Work with local Aboriginal Elders on caring for the creek

b.q: A council is planning a new suburb in Western Sydney, on land with a creek running through it. It wants the plan to care for Country. Which step would best do this?
opts: Learn from local Elders about this creek and its plants
Ask Elders to sign off on a plan to pipe the creek
Copy the creek design from a suburb in another state
Let developers choose where the creek is moved to
b.why: Learning from local Elders brings in knowledge of this particular place, such as how its waters and plants have been cared for. Asking Elders only to approve a finished plan does not use their knowledge, and piping the creek removes the waterway instead of caring for it.
b.clue: Which step draws on knowledge of this particular place?
